_readme: Policy for safety-guard.cjs. Edit THIS file to change what is blocked —
no JavaScript required. Detection lives in the .cjs; which operations your
team protects is policy, and policy belongs in data.
your team's equivalents (keep the base name only — `test-results`,
Each rule: name (appears in the message), pattern (JS regex source, matched
against the whole shell command), flags (default 'i'), action, reason, and
for deny rules a safe alternative the agent can recover with.
action: "deny" — never legitimate from an agent. Hard block.
action: "ask"  — legitimate work that must not happen silently. Prompts you.
The deny/ask split is the whole design. A guard that hard-blocks routine work
gets switched off, and a switched-off guard protects nothing. Deny what is
never right; ask about what is sometimes right.
exemptWhenSafeDelete: true — the rule is skipped when every path the command
targets has a basename in safeDeleteTargets. This is what keeps
`rm -rf node_modules` from being the false positive that gets the hook deleted.
PAIRED FILE: this file and safety-guard.cjs ship together. The hook fails
open (with a warning) when the policy is missing, so installing one without
the other leaves the guard inert. `ko-dev-kit init` copies both.
This file is merge-protected on kit updates: your edits are kept and the
kit's new version lands beside it as destructive-rules.json.kit-update.

rules.name: force-push
rules.alternative: use --force-with-lease if a force push is truly intended

rules.name: force-push-short-flag
rules.alternative: use --force-with-lease if a force push is truly intended

rules.name: force-push-with-lease
rules.reason: a lease-guarded force push still rewrites the remote branch — it must not happen silently
rules.alternative: confirm the user intends to rewrite the remote branch

rules.name: reset-hard
rules.alternative: git stash (or commit to a scratch branch) keeps the work recoverable

rules.name: clean-force
rules.reason: git clean -f deletes untracked files irreversibly
rules.alternative: git stash -u, or list targets first with git clean -n

rules.name: checkout-discard
rules.alternative: git stash keeps the work recoverable

rules.name: recursive-force-delete
rules.reason: rm -rf against a broad target can wipe the workspace
rules.alternative: delete a specific subdirectory, and prefer moving to /tmp over deleting

rules.name: publish-from-shell
rules.reason: publishing from a local shell bypasses release checks
rules.alternative: publish via the repo release workflow / CI

rules.name: sudo-delete
rules.reason: privileged filesystem operations are out of scope for an agent
rules.alternative: ask the user to run it themselves if they are sure

rules.name: raw-device-write
rules.reason: writing to a raw device destroys a disk — there is no recovery
rules.alternative: none from an agent; the user runs this by hand

rules.name: chmod-world-writable
rules.alternative: grant the narrowest mode that works (644 for files, 755 for directories)

rules.name: remote-script-execution
rules.reason: piping a downloaded script straight into a shell runs unreviewed code
rules.alternative: download it, read it, then run it

rules.name: git-history-rewrite
rules.reason: rewriting published history breaks every clone
rules.alternative: coordinate history changes with the team out of band
